title: 35.3 A 30MHz Wideband 92.7dB SNR 99.6% Accuracy Bioimpedance Spectroscopy IC Using Time-to-Digital Demodulation with Co-Prime Delay Locked Sampling
problem: Wideband bioimpedance spectroscopy up to 30MHz requires high SNR (>90dB) and phase accuracy (<0.6°) for biological assessment (fluid volume, cancer diagnosis, plant composition), but existing ICs are limited to 10MHz with analog I-Q demodulation suffering from 4+ degree phase errors.
motivation: 30MHz spectroscopy enables detection of α, β, and γ dispersions in tissue permittivity/conductivity; applications like cassava starch measurement require previously unavailable frequency coverage.
method: Instead of conventional I-Q mixing (multiplying the signal by two reference signals), this IC uses time-to-digital demodulation, which converts signal timing into digital information for measurement. It achieves high phase accuracy through co-prime delay-locked sampling (a technique where precisely timed delays stack to simulate a much faster sampling rate), reaching 21.6GHz effective sampling from a 240MHz clock. A phase comparator-based delay-locked loop generates these accurate delays, while an optimized wideband current generator and front-end design handle frequencies up to 30MHz. This design eliminates the distortion caused by analog multiplication in conventional systems.
key_novelty: The core idea is using time-to-digital demodulation with co-prime delay-locked sampling to measure phase accurately across a wide frequency range without the distortion that traditional analog I-Q multiplication causes.
contributions: Co-prime delay-locked sampling technique achieving 21.6GHz equivalent sampling from 240MHz clock
92.7dB SNR with 99.6% accuracy (0.39% magnitude error, 0.57° phase error at 30MHz)
Low power consumption (3.18mW) vs. prior digital I-Q approach (12.2mW ADC+amplifier)
baselines: Analog I-Q demodulation (4.32° phase error at 10MHz)
primary_theme: Wideband bioimpedance spectroscopy via time-to-digital demodulation with co-prime delay-locked sampling
